headline: Find the cycle entrance using Floyd’s two phases
statement: Return the original node where a singly linked list’s cycle begins, or None if there is no cycle. The input fixture uses pos as the tail’s connection index; pos is not a parameter of detectCycle. Do not modify the list.
constraints: pos is -1 for no cycle or an existing zero-based index
intuition: Moving one and two steps detects a cycle because their relative position changes by one per round. At a meeting, the number of steps taken by slow is a multiple of the cycle length. Resetting one pointer to head lets both meet at the entrance when moved equally.
approach: Advance slow by one and fast by two until they meet or fast reaches the end.
On a meeting, reset an entrance pointer to head.
Move entrance and slow one step at a time until their identities match.
correctness: Let the entrance be μ links from head, the meeting be x links into a cycle of length λ, and slow’s meeting distance be t. Fast has travelled 2t, so their distance difference t is a multiple of λ; t=μ+x modulo λ gives μ=-x modulo λ. Thus a pointer from head and a pointer from the meeting reach the entrance together after μ steps. An acyclic list makes fast reach None.
bruteForce: Store visited node identities in a set; the first repeated node is the entrance, requiring O(n) space.

complexity.explanation: Detection and entrance localization each walk at most a constant multiple of the number of distinct nodes.

pitfalls: Compare node identities, not equal values.
Guard fast.next before taking two steps.
